claims.assertion: Devin by Cognition claims to have raised $21 million (source text: "raised a $21 million Series A led by Founders Fund").

evidence.snippet: Cognition, the makers of the autonomous AI software engineer named Devin, has raised more than $1 billion at a $25 billion pre-money valuation ($26 billion post money), the company announced on Wednesday.

Palo Alto–based startup Cognition, founded in 2022 by Roshun Patel, Ndeye Thiam and Sachin Sudarsanam, raised a $200 million Series A led by Lightspeed in September 2023, valuing the company above $2 billion after earlier seed and Kickstarter ...
Motivation Behind the Round: To expand the engineering team and enhance product capabilities following rapid traction with Devin.
Just a month after announcing a $21 million Series A round, Cognition AI, a startup developing an AI-powered coding assistant called Devin, has raised another $175 million led by Founders Fund.

claims.notes: Funding reports are wildly contradictory, ranging from $21M to $1B+; the lack of a single consistent figure makes the specific claim unverifiable.

verdict: The company's claims regarding its product and technical capabilities are well-corroborated by the industry. However, the financial reporting surrounding the company is chaotic and contradictory, with massive discrepancies in funding figures that remain impossible to reconcile. The product itself is clearly real, but the financial narrative is deeply sus.
